### 6.2 Statistics
| Test | Exact statistic and rule |
| Losses | With y' = max(y, 1e-12) and f' = max(f, 1e-12): QLIKE = y'/f' - log(y'/f') - 1, log-MSE = (log y' - log f')^2 |

| Long-lag p (descriptive) | The same S with Bartlett lags 1 to 240 (10 calendar days of 1h windows). Never gates |

Abs funding and abs premium on H may lie outside their D training ranges, and the linear terms extrapolate with no clipping (neither M nor draft 5 has a clipping rule). - D's descriptive refit comparison found monthly refitting better (+0.0147 QLIKE, 90% interval [0.0041, 0.0329]). H tests the model without refit.
- Lag-1 HAC understates the DM standard error when loss differentials stay correlated (draft 5's disclosure, size 31.8% on a synthetic phi 0.9 case). The long-lag p is reported beside each gated p.

- Draft 5's zero-volume rule applies on H as on D. Each voided window removes up to 30 days of the coin's forecasts, so voids recurring at intervals under 30 days remove a coin's forecasts entirely (Opus, synthetic: one void every 17 days removed every forecast of that coin). The number of such bars on H is unknown before the read, and genuine no-trade 5m bars in a thin early listing would void windows like exchange placeholders do (OD8).

- Condition 2's cost bound is A1.1's 2026 schedule, not the schedule in force in 2020 and 2021, and its Brownian range mapping is approximate (draft 5).
- As on D, a forecast row exists only where its window is complete, because evaluation needs y. Flag 1's trailing percentile is taken over those rows, as on D.

- The H batch rule (one apply_fit call per coin over its complete windows) makes the last bits of f at T depend on which later windows are complete, as compute_forecasts' batch did within each D month. It cannot change the verdict short of an exact tie at a threshold.
- `family_c.run_holdout`'s docstring says "t1 at or before DEV_END minus 30 days". Draft 5 and `fit_fold` use t1 strictly before the cutoff, which governs. The docstring is frozen and stays.

## 14. Signature
- The signature lives in the lock record's `signature` field, `{"by", "date", "session", "text_sha256"}`, which the lock-record tool writes when the owner signs.

- The text cannot carry its own sha256. The signature covers the text whose sha256 is recorded in `text_sha256` of the lock record, repeated in `signature.text_sha256`: the sha256 over the UTF-8 bytes of the record's `text` lines joined by a line feed, with no trailing line feed. The tool refuses a text with a carriage return or a blank last line.

- The text is this file as the owner signs it. The signing commit adds the lock record and the artifact copy, changes nothing under `scripts/research/py/r4/`, and its sha is the read id (section 3.1).
